content:
Ben Carter: early look at onboarding email v2 A/B (Email #1) from last 24h. sharing bc we need to decide: extend test window vs ship winner.

Ben Carter: Setup recap:
- Audience: net-new self-serve signups (Hosted API), excluding existing workspaces + suppressed enterprise opp domains list
- Split: 50/50, cohort-assigned via lifecycle_growth_email_v2 flag
- Variant A = “get to first token fast” subject + shorter body + single CTA (Run first request)
- Variant B = “cut inference cost” subject + longer body + 2 CTAs (Quickstart + Console)
- Success metrics: opens/clicks + downstream activation (first_success_request within 7d; first_100k_tokens within 7d)

Ben Carter: Snapshot (as of ~10am PT, n=2,412 delivered total):
- Open rate: A 51.8% vs B 47.1% (+4.7pp)
- Click rate (unique): A 13.9% vs B 10.4% (+3.5pp)
- Click-to-open: A 26.8% vs B 22.1%
- Unsub: A 0.18% vs B 0.16% (basically flat)
- Complaints: 0 so far (low volume, but good)

Ben Carter: Downstream (caveat: still early, 7d window not mature):
- first_success_request within 48h of signup: A 34.6% vs B 31.9% (+2.7pp)
- first_100k_tokens within 48h: A 9.4% vs B 8.8% (+0.6pp)

Ben Carter: I’m leaning “extend another 48–72h” to avoid calling it too early. But A looks pretty clearly better on opens/clicks + early activation. Thoughts?

Tyler Benson: thx. I pulled the same in the funnel dashboard (growth > lifecycle > email_v2). direction matches.

Tyler Benson: 2 notes:
1) for downstream, 48h is noisy but at least it’s apples-to-apples. we should also look at “API key created” as an earlier indicator (less lag than first_success_request).
2) clicks are tracking fine (UTMs consistent), but there’s some “console CTA” leakage bc folks can go straight to console after clicking docs. not a blocker, just don’t over-interpret path.

Tyler Benson: if we want stats confidence, I’d suggest run until we hit ~5k delivered per arm OR end of day Monday, whichever first. right now p-values aren’t stable.

Soojin Lee: copy-wise this makes sense. A’s value prop is clearer (one job: make a first request).

Soojin Lee: B’s subject “cut cost” is a little aspirational for day-0 user. they don’t believe cost matters yet because they haven’t shipped anything.

Soojin Lee: if we do ship A, please keep B’s second paragraph that mentions reliability / “predictable latency” (it was strong). but keep the single CTA.

Camila Reyes: what’s the downside of extending? any deliverability risk from holding back the “winner”?

Ben Carter: downside is mostly time. we’re in Week 1 and want to roll learnings into Email #2 + console nudge copy. but we can parallelize.

Ben Carter: deliverability-wise, both variants are same sender + same volume. no risk from extending A/B itself. risk is just “we move slower.”

Tyler Benson: +1. also: if we swap too quickly and it’s regression later, we’ll have a harder time diagnosing.

Camila Reyes: ok. but if opens/clicks are already clearly better, why not just roll A to 80/20 and keep a holdout?

Tyler Benson: we can do that. 80/20 lets us keep learning while capturing most upside. but we should be strict about cohort assignment so we don’t contaminate.

Ben Carter: I’m fine with 80/20 starting tomorrow AM. keep B as 20% for continued measurement thru Monday.

Michael Grant: quick compliance check: any changes to suppression / unsubscribe handling tied to the experiment? just making sure we’re not changing operational behavior between arms.

Ben Carter: no changes between arms. both include footer + unsubscribe link, and suppression rules are shared (global opt-out + hard bounces).

Michael Grant: ok great.

Soojin Lee: if we go 80/20, pls confirm the variant naming in the ESP matches what’s in the readout doc. last sprint we had “A/B” vs “control/treatment” mismatch and it was a mess.

Tyler Benson: yep I’ll update the mapping doc + dashboard labels today. also adding API key created as a secondary chart.

Ben Carter: Decision proposal:
- Move to 80/20 in favor of A starting tomorrow 9am PT
- Keep B 20% until Monday EOD (or until 5k/arm) for confidence
- Use A copy as baseline for Email #2 drafting now (Soojin to review)

Ben Carter: objections?

Camila Reyes: no objections. please add a stop/go note: if unsub or complaint rate spikes above guardrail, revert to 50/50 or pause.

Tyler Benson: guardrails I’ve got:
- complaint rate >0.08% in 24h = pause sends + investigate
- unsub >0.8% in 24h = review content + targeting
- bounce rate >2% = deliverability check

Ben Carter: cool. action items:
- Tyler: change split + update dashboard labels + add API key chart
- Soojin: fold in reliability line to A (keep single CTA)
- Ben: update Week 1 readout doc w/ new plan + ping #announcements after change

Ben Carter: (reactions: :thumbsup: from Camila Reyes, Soojin Lee, Tyler Benson)
